claims.statement: JUCE Normalise is energy-based (0.125 / sqrt(hottest-channel-energy)) — used for reverb IRs so an IR's absolute level means nothing. Short IRs (≤ 1 s, cab class) instead get a −18 dB output pad (computeIrNormalizationGain) with 100% default mix; long IRs (> 1 s, reverb class) use Normalise with 50% default mix. kMaxIrSeconds = 10.0 is a hard cap on loaded IR length; kShortIrMaxBaseSamples = 48000 (1 s at the 48 kHz base rate); kLongIrDefaultMix = 0.5.

The IR convolver runs at the base (chain) rate, NOT the host rate: IR blocks are rate-isolated islands inside the 48 kHz chain domain (ChainDomain's boundary resampler re-samples host↔chain at the chain edges). This is why BudgetConvolver's sample-count constants (kFrame=8192, kMaxCall=256) refer to 48 kHz samples even when the host runs 96/192 kHz — the convolver never sees host-rate samples.

BudgetConvolver (plugin/include/effects/conv/BudgetConvolver.h; formerly flat plugin/include/BudgetConvolver.h before the per-effect subdirectory move) is a bounded per-call OLA long-tail convolver: it does the same per-pair math as JUCE's non-uniform engine (real-only FFT 16384, verbatim JUCE packed-domain product: prepareForConvolution / convolutionProcessingAndAccumulate / updateSymmetricFrequencyDomainData) — the difference is schedule. JUCE (processSamplesWithAddedLatency) pays FWD FFT + all N outstanding (frame×seg) products + IFFT in ONE boundary call once per 8192 input samples — worse the longer the IR; BudgetConvolver pays one 16384-point real transform + one new (frame×seg0) product in one call, defers the IFFT to the NEXT call, and bounds steady-state calls to K old products (K = ceil(M / callsMax), M = tailSamples/8192 + 1). Heaviest call ≈ one 16384-pt real transform (~0.35 ms 2-ch), well under 1.0 ms.

kIrConvolverMaxBlockSize = 256 (ChainBlock.h) caps the per-call BudgetConvolver feed; irConvolverBlockSizeFor and processConvolverInChunks (ChainBlock.h) split any host-sized block into ≤256-sample slices so per-call OLA product cost cannot inflate with the host's block size — the host block may be larger than the cap but the product budget per call stays bounded regardless. BudgetConvolver.h (now in plugin/include/effects/conv/) carries the matching kMaxCall = 256 / kFrame = 8192 pair as its own copy of the house CPU law (ConvolutionReverb.h references this cap in its header comment: 'Block-size cap (kIrConvolverMaxBlockSize) + chunked RT feed').

ConvolutionReverb (IR-driven plate reverb; now plugin/include/effects/conv/ConvolutionReverb.h) shares this engine: a ~150 ms install-fade warmup (JUCE's dry crossfade elapses off the live path by feeding the fresh tail one silence frame at rebuild — ConvolutionReverb.cpp ~325-327, `cold.clear()` then `tail->process(cold)` — not at first wet; the dedicated message-thread `primeSilence` warm-up was removed in the 2026-10-20 optimization-findings Stage 5 as a zero-caller), and the JUCE non-uniform OLA replaced by the BudgetConvolver tail. Reverb-specific: user time-stretch (JUCE re-samples the edited IR to engine rate), 4.0 quad→stereo downmix folded BEFORE JUCE sees it (L=(c0+c2)/√2, R=(c1+c3)/√2 — JUCE reads only ch 0/1 and would drop the rear pair), and JUCE Normalise on the load path. The mod layer writes the wet ring through a one-pole smoother (kModWriteTauMs=80, 44a78ea) so repeated LFO passes never re-emit raw wet transients (the periodic click; see the mod claim below).

The conv wet path ends in a stateless soft-knee peak limiter (process stage 3c, ConvolutionReverb.cpp:845-849, gated by clipEnabled_, NOT applied on the dying crossfade tail): a 1024-entry LUT over log|x| in [kClipLogLo=-6.9, kClipLogHi=5.3], law H(u) = 2.2886 + (-5.1009*u - 9.6838)*T with T = smoothstep((u + 1.4498)/4.4287) — floor lift kClipFloorDb=2.2886 dB at low levels, knee at x≈kClipKneeX=0.2231, ceiling kClipCeilingGain=1.3232 (1/|x| roll above it). The LUT is filled with juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain (a plain e^(db/20) fill is a constant -1.29 dB bug). No user knob, not part of state, and deliberately EXCLUDED from IR export. Law guarded by WetClipCurveLaw + WetClipInPath in test/src/convolution_reverb_tests.cpp (plain 0.3 dB tolerance); the 7 pre-clip contract tests call setClipEnabledForTest(false).

Kernel export (commit 89afb4e): ConvolutionReverb::exportKernel(targetRate, &error) (ConvolutionReverb.h:336, cpp:390) re-runs the SAME makeEditedState linear pipeline — trim (convStartS/convEndS) + stretch (Time) + fades/curves — at the raw file rate, then resamples to the target rate and bakes the linear stages: Pre zero-pad, Gain (pow(10, gainToDb/20)), Width (stereo M/S fold; mono IR = Haas interaural delay pair, kHaasDelayMs, side = width*kHaasDepth*delayed). Mod and the wet soft clip are live-only and deliberately not baked. The result is always 2-channel (mono duplicated). TONE3000Processor::exportConvIr (ProcessorChain.cpp:481) wraps it: bits clamped 16..32, WavAudioFormat writer over a file OutputStream (the juce::MemoryOutputStream 0-byte trap class), deletes the file on failure. Guarded by ConvIrExport* tests (convolution_reverb_tests.cpp) + the exportConvIr WAV round-trip (processor_tests.cpp).

Mod wet-ring click fix (commit 44a78ea, spec spc-1792538043915-13755): when the Mod knob is up, the ring-tap path re-emitted the wet signal's transients once per LFO pass, producing a periodic click. The fix smooths the wet RING WRITE (not the tap read) with a causal one-pole: ConvolutionReverb.h kModWriteTauMs=80.0 (public law constant; test hooks setModWriteTauForTest(ms)/modWriteTauForTest(), <0 disables = raw write so the disabled path stays bit-exact against the pre-fix anchor, 0 = ship default); process() recomputes modSmCoef_=exp(-1/(rate*wMs*1e-3)) per call and writes modSmPrev_[c]=coef*modSmPrev_[c]+(1-coef)*wet[i] INTO the ring before the taps read it (write-before-read keeps the current sample causal — zero latency preserved, no look-ahead, no oversampling). Prepare zeros modSmPrev_[2]. The taps/lengths/gain law are unchanged, so with Mod=0 the ring write is the raw wet (identical to before). Guarded by the click-index / tap-body gtests added at 44a78ea in test/src/convolution_reverb_tests.cpp (DspTests 579/579).
